name: Tumours of the Ear and Cerebellopontine Angle

reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Unilateral SNHL plus tinnitus: MRI excludes schwannoma
Pulsatile tinnitus plus red retrotympanic mass equals glomus
Meningioma is second commonest CPA tumour with dural tail
Facial preservation is prime surgical metric in CPA surgery
reference.pathophysiology: Slow Schwann cell proliferation expands the meatus and angle cistern compressing cochlear nerve first; paraganglioma vascular nests grow along skull base foramina eroding bone while fed by ascending pharyngeal vessels.
additionalDifferentials: Schwannoma versus meningioma imaging (meatal expansion versus dural tail)
Glomus tympanicum (middle ear only) versus jugulare (foramen erosion)
Epidermoid diffusion restriction versus arachnoid cyst following CSF
additionalInvestigations: Gadolinium MRI internal meatus and CPA
CT temporal bone for glomus bone erosion; angiography and embolisation planning
